messages.content: Write a job posting for a senior backend engineer at a mid-sized fintech company. Around 250 words.

**Senior Backend Engineer**
Payments Platform · Chicago or remote (US) · $190–225k + equity

We move money. About $4B a year, mostly ACH and card settlement for small business lenders, and the code that does it is a Go monolith with a Postgres database that has strong opinions about correctness.

You'd own the ledger service. That means double-entry accounting primitives, idempotency across retries, and reconciliation jobs that have to agree with what the bank says by 6am. When they disagree, someone reads the audit log. Lately that someone is one exhausted staff engineer, which is why we're hiring. The work is less about scale than about being right. Our peak is 3,000 transactions a minute. Nobody has ever paged us about latency. We get paged when a partner's file format changes at midnight and 400 disbursements land in the wrong state.

Here's what we're looking for. Six or more years writing backend services, some of it in Go, Java, or Rust. You've designed a schema that outlived you. Real experience with financial data, or a strong argument for why you'd pick it up fast. Comfort with on-call, which runs one week in six and is quiet most weeks.

Some things we are not. We're 140 people, profitable since 2023, and we do not have a research team. If you want to work on distributed consensus from first principles, this isn't the job. If you want to make a payments system boring, it is.

Two interviews, one of them a code reading session on our actual repo. We pay for take-homes. No whiteboards.

Write to careers@[company].com — a paragraph is fine, no cover letter.

Details are invented placeholders. Swap in your real volumes, comp band, stack, and process before posting.

The text above has these problems. Rewrite it so none remain.
Change nothing else, and keep the same length and purpose.

- bold_density:

Return only the rewritten text.
